correctness.rationale: For N>=2 and all positive masses, internal springs and independently varying inter-dimer stiffnesses, M^(-1/2) K M^(-1/2) is an irreducible Jacobi matrix, so positive eigenvalues are simple and smoothly ordered. Hellmann-Feynman gives partial lambda_j / partial b_i=(u_(B_i)-u_(A_(i+1)))^2 (mass-normalized). Thus joint stationarity forces all inter-dimer elongations zero; restricting every internal dimer to its local optical eigenproblem and connectivity of the free path shows all local squared optical frequencies coincide. Conversely an explicit recurrence u_(B_i)=-(alpha_i/beta_i) u_(A_i), u_(A_(i+1))=u_(B_i) constructs an exact b-independent vector for all b_i>0, with eigenvalue Lambda. N sign changes across internal bonds yield simple ordinal N+1 by Jacobi Sturm oscillation. Independently assembled and mass-normalized 36 randomly heterogeneous chains N=2,3,5 and verified residuals and correct sorted eigenvalue index. No claim of uniform spectral gap or invariance under mass/internal-spring changes.

value.rationale: The iff pinning criterion characterizes when a free mechanical chain has an exactly robust eigenfrequency and mode shape under an (N-1)-parameter family of independent positive spring perturbations, identifying its exact spectral order. It is a natural structural invariant and design boundary, not a small numerical improvement; it clearly separates robustness to intercell stiffness from mass and intracell detuning.
